record.paper_title: Some Properties of and Open Problems on Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials
record.context_brief: Whether self-inverting series are automatically Hessian nilpotent
record.original_question: Let P(z) be a formal power series in C[[z]] with order at least 2 and with (Hes P)(0) nilpotent. Define its symmetric formal map F(z) = z - grad P(z); when the inverse has the form G(z) = z + grad Q(z), call Q(z) the inversion pair of P(z). If P is self-inverting, meaning Q(z) = P(z), must every such self-inverting polynomial or formal power series be Hessian nilpotent?

evidence.quote: there exists a unique Qt (z) in C[[t]][[z]] with o(Qt (z)) >= 2 such that Gt (z) = z + t grad Qt (z). We call Qt (z) the deformed inversion pair of P (z).
Definition 4.1. A formal power series P (z) in C[[z]] with o(P (z)) >= 2 and (Hes P )(0) nilpotent is said to be self-inverting if its inversion pair Q(z) = P (z).
Open Problem 4.8. (a) Decide whether or not all self-inverting polynomials or formal power series are HN.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the formal power series ring $\mathbb{C}[[z]] = \mathbb{C}[[z_1, \dots, z_n]]$. For $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$, let $o(P)$ denote the order (lowest degree of a nonzero monomial), $\nabla P = (\partial P/\partial z_1, \dots, \partial P/\partial z_n)$ the gradient, and $\mathrm{Hes}(P) = (\partial^2 P/\partial z_i \partial z_j)$ the Hessian matrix. Call $P$ Hessian nilpotent (HN) if $\mathrm{Hes}(P)$ is a nilpotent matrix over $\mathbb{C}[[z]]$.

Assume $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ satisfies $o(P) \ge 2$ and $(\mathrm{Hes}\,P)(0)$ is nilpotent. Define the symmetric formal map
$$F(z) = z - \nabla P(z).$$
Under these hypotheses one can show that $F$ has a formal inverse $G(z)$ and that $G(z)$ can be uniquely written in the form
$$G(z) = z + \nabla Q(z)$$
for some $Q(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ with $o(Q) \ge 2$. The series $Q(z)$ is called the inversion pair of $P(z)$.

Say that $P(z)$ is self-inverting if $Q(z) = P(z)$.

Question: must every self-inverting polynomial (or, more generally, every self-inverting formal power series) $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ necessarily be Hessian nilpotent?
artifact.status_search_result: A search returned the original problem listing and related work on Hessian nilpotent polynomials and the Jacobian conjecture, but no source was found that resolves whether every self-inverting polynomial or formal power series must be Hessian nilpotent. The problem appears to remain unresolved, but no definitive recent statement was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Results on homogeneous HN polynomials, but no resolution of the self-inverting question.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work on HN polynomials does not appear to settle this specific question.
